title: Painful crisis in sickle cell disease — recognise danger, assess and act safely

blocks.text: Painful crisis in sickle cell disease — recognise danger, assess and act safely

AMaC MRCP PACES23 · Round 5 · R5-211 · Station 2 acute consultation · 20 minutes · Assessed skills: A clinical assessment, B physical signs where appropriate, C communication, D differential diagnosis, E clinical judgement, F patient concerns, G welfare · Not an official PACES mark scheme.

A 24-year-old with sickle cell disease presents in severe limb and back pain, consistent with previous painful episodes. Conduct the initial consultation and agree a safe management plan. You are the medical registrar in the acute assessment unit (or appropriately designated acute clinician). Explore concerns, assess risk and explain the immediate plan.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: Hook: Acute painful sickle cell episode, but exclude acute chest syndrome, infection, osteomyelitis, stroke and other causes of atypical pain. Examiner trap: New chest symptoms, fever or oxygen saturation ≤95% can signal acute chest syndrome; immediate medical review and targeted work-up are necessary. Avoid fluid overload and routine oxygen in normal saturation.

Acute painful sickle cell episode, but exclude acute chest syndrome, infection, osteomyelitis, stroke and other causes of atypical pain.

Give suitable analgesia within 30 minutes of presentation; use the individual plan and reassess pain every 30 minutes until relief. Encourage oral fluids or judicious IV fluids if needed; give oxygen if hypoxaemic.

blocks.text: Patient is anxious but cooperative. Open with: “I am worried something serious is happening.” Answer history questions using these facts only: Assess pain score, timing and usual care plan, temperature, pulse, respiratory rate and room-air oxygen saturation; ask specifically about chest pain, cough, breathlessness and new neurological signs. Ask “Will I need to stay in hospital?” and accept calm, specific explanations. No unscripted extra examination findings.

Q1: How soon is analgesia offered?
Expected answer: Within 30 minutes of hospital presentation.

Q2: What monitors matter?
Expected answer: Pain score, BP, HR, RR, temperature, SpO2 and sedation if strong opioids used.

Q3: Is oxygen universal?
Expected answer: No: NICE CG143 recommends offering oxygen if SpO2 is 95% or below.

Q4: What is avoided?
Expected answer: Do not offer pethidine; corticosteroids are not for uncomplicated crisis.

Q5: Which complication needs urgent evaluation?
Expected answer: Acute chest syndrome with new chest symptoms, fever or hypoxia.
